<compartment start="138" end="146" title="Moved synonym rollout to shadow index" episode_type="infra,refactor" importance="58">
<p1>
Reworked how the Atlas search stack ships synonym changes after the last in-place reload caused a lunchtime latency spike. search/indexer/src/synonyms/reload.ts no longer patches the hot index directly; instead it builds a shadow index, loads the synonym set there, warms the query cache, and then swaps aliases. terraform/opensearch/synonym_sets.tf and docs/search/release.md were updated to treat synonym changes the same way schema promotions already work. Commit 73ce4ad.
</p1>
<p2>
Atlas search now rolls out synonym changes through a shadow-index promotion instead of mutating the live index in place. That keeps synonym updates on the same safer path as schema changes.
</p2>
<p3>
Synonym edits are now shipped by building and promoting a shadow index, not by reloading the hot one.
</p3>
<p4>products_live; products_next; shadow-index synonym rollout</p4>
</compartment>
<facts>
<PROJECT_RULES>
* Search schema changes and synonym changes ship through the same shadow-index promotion workflow.
</PROJECT_RULES>
<ARCHITECTURE>
* Synonym changes are applied by building a shadow index and swapping aliases, not by reloading the hot index in place.
</ARCHITECTURE>
<NAMING>
* The paired search aliases are products_live and products_next.
</NAMING>
</facts>

<compartment start="224" end="231" title="Ledger: invoice_status column rename reversed after reporting breakage" episode_type="bug" importance="7">
<p1>
Renamed invoice_status column to status in the invoices table as cosmetic cleanup (migration 0047_rename_invoice_status.sql). Two hours later all scheduled overnight reports came back empty.

U: "why are all the reports empty this morning"

Traced to the reporting service using raw SQL with column name invoice_status — not through the ORM. Missed in review because the reporting service lives in a separate repo. Reverted via migration 0048_revert_rename.sql, commit 1f0e52a. Rename deferred until the reporting service can be updated in the same coordinated changeset.
</p1>

<compartment start="415" end="612" title="Tenant isolation: chose Postgres RLS over schema-per-tenant" episode_type="design" importance="94">
<p1>
Worked through the tenant isolation model for the new control plane. Three candidates on the table: (a) schema-per-tenant with `search_path` switching, (b) database-per-tenant, (c) shared schema with Postgres Row-Level Security policies keyed on `tenant_id`. Spent the morning sketching how each interacts with our migration tooling, connection pooling (pgbouncer in transaction mode), and the analytics replica.

U: I keep getting pulled toward schema-per-tenant because it feels "more isolated" but I want to be talked out of it if RLS holds up

Schema-per-tenant blows up under pgbouncer transaction-pooling — `SET search_path` is session-state and gets lost between transactions; the per-tenant search_path either has to be set on every transaction (expensive, race-prone) or we drop pgbouncer (kills our connection economy). Database-per-tenant solves isolation cleanly but our migration tooling (sqlx) doesn't have a clean fan-out story and we'd need to build one. Also onboarding latency goes from ~50ms to ~30s because we'd need to provision a DB.

Landed on RLS. Every tenant-scoped table gets `tenant_id uuid not null`, an `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` declaration, and a policy `USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.current_tenant')::uuid)`. The current tenant is set via `SET LOCAL app.current_tenant = '...'` at the start of every request transaction — `SET LOCAL` is transaction-scoped so it survives pgbouncer transaction mode cleanly. Wrote a middleware in `internal/db/tenant.go` that wraps every request in a transaction and sets the value.

U: what about the analytics replica, does RLS work the same there

Yes — RLS policies replicate via logical replication; the analytics service connects with a separate role that also has RLS enforced. The escape hatch for cross-tenant analytics is a dedicated `analytics_admin` role with `BYPASSRLS`, used only by the scheduled aggregation job, never by interactive code paths.

U: ok and write down that if anyone ever calls SET ROLE to escape RLS in app code i'm going to lose my mind

Documented. Added a lint rule in `tools/sqllint/` that flags `SET ROLE`, `BYPASSRLS`, and unqualified table access in `internal/handlers/`.
</p1>
<p2>
Tenant isolation decision: Postgres RLS keyed on `tenant_id`, set per-transaction via `SET LOCAL app.current_tenant`. Rejected schema-per-tenant (breaks pgbouncer transaction mode) and database-per-tenant (sqlx migration fan-out cost + 30s onboarding latency). Analytics uses a separate role with BYPASSRLS for the scheduled aggregator only. U: "if anyone ever calls SET ROLE to escape RLS in app code i'm going to lose my mind." Lint rule added in `tools/sqllint/`.
</p2>
<p3>
Chose RLS with `tenant_id` and `SET LOCAL app.current_tenant` per request. BYPASSRLS reserved for the scheduled analytics aggregator role only; app code is lint-enforced to never bypass.
</p3>
<p4>
RLS on tenant_id; SET LOCAL app.current_tenant; BYPASSRLS = analytics_admin only
</p4>
</compartment>
<facts>
<ARCHITECTURE>
* Tenant isolation is enforced at the database layer via Postgres RLS keyed on `tenant_id`, not via schema separation. Chosen because `SET LOCAL` is transaction-scoped and survives pgbouncer transaction-mode pooling, where session-scoped `search_path` switching does not.
</ARCHITECTURE>
<PROJECT_RULES>
* Every tenant-scoped table must declare `tenant_id uuid not null` and `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` with a policy referencing `current_setting('app.current_tenant')`.
* Application code must never call `SET ROLE` or use `BYPASSRLS` roles. `tools/sqllint/` enforces this in CI.
</PROJECT_RULES>
<CONSTRAINTS>
* `SET search_path` is session-scoped and is silently lost between transactions when running behind pgbouncer in transaction pooling mode — making schema-per-tenant impractical for our deployment.
</CONSTRAINTS>
<CONFIG_VALUES>
* Per-request tenant context is set via `SET LOCAL app.current_tenant = '<uuid>'` inside the request transaction opened by `internal/db/tenant.go`.
</CONFIG_VALUES>
<NAMING>
* The privileged analytics role is `analytics_admin` (the only role with `BYPASSRLS`); used exclusively by the scheduled aggregation job.
</NAMING>
</facts>
<events>
<trajectory_correction at_compartment="3">
  <summary>Considered and rejected schema-per-tenant in favor of RLS after realizing it was incompatible with the existing pgbouncer setup.</summary>
  <before_strategy>Lean toward schema-per-tenant for "stronger" isolation feel.</before_strategy>
  <correction_source>self_review</correction_source>
  <correction_signal>Realized `SET search_path` is session-scoped and doesn't survive pgbouncer transaction-mode pooling.</correction_signal>

</trajectory_correction>

<compartment start="55" end="58" title="Fixed reliable_new cross-cycle stall (D-E2E-1) + 总协调 six-item ruling" episode_type="bug" importance="78">
<p1>
I dispatched a fix for defect D-E2E-1: when `assessment.analyze` re-ran with a fresh process/double, the search still reported `reliable_new` even though our own prior enrollment had already created the member row, so the handler re-enqueued and raised `IDENTITY_ENROLLMENT_PENDING` forever. The fix computes `candidate_id = candidate_entity_id(ns, assessment_id)` and reconciles against PG: if a member exists, it sets `member_id` and `identity_result = {"schema_version":1,"classification":"reliable_new","phase":"enrolled_reconciled","candidate_entity_id":…,"member_id":…}` and falls through to the normal publish path; if absent it delegates to `_handle_reliable_new` exactly as before. The MATCHED-from-search path was untouched. 95 tests green, and I verified the new test genuinely covers the defect by temporarily forcing `reconciled_member_id = None` (the test failed as expected, then I restored the fix).

Then 总协调 sent a six-item incremental ruling on the coordination request and authoritative MD:

U: 媒体边界原则接受，术语改"授权可读集合"，不是公网公开；必须全量校验可信云台主体、当前指针、冻结报告引用及照片版本。

U: namespace级稳定UUID串行符合DD，保留确定性与未决登记阻塞，不改A helper。

U: 必须纠正 requiredViews：failure_detail 已确认仅内部诊断列，数据架构通用约束禁止用于业务决策或跨服务协议，不得从它投影 requiredViews。

U: 暂不接受等待方案：正常缺少能力不得每30秒generation_revision+1并创建succeeded后继任务。

U: media.cleanup 明确属于MVP，归D补齐最小handler及验证证据，不因D编号清单遗漏将其留作UNSUPPORTED_CONTRACT。

Item 1 accepted the media boundary but renamed the concept to "授权可读集合" (authorized-readable set), not public; item 2 kept the namespace-level deterministic UUID serialization and said not to change A's helper; item 3 forbade projecting requiredViews from `failure_detail` and required it to move into the existing versioned business JSON (identity_result); item 4 rejected the 30s wait-hop entirely — keep the same generation revision and logical task, use a lease-fenced deferral that doesn't consume a failed attempt, and don't rely on infinite successor jobs; item 5 assigned `media.cleanup` to D (minimal handler + verification evidence, idempotent, checking all T05/T01/T07/T13 references, no TTL on real data); item 6 accepted the remaining boundaries (initial generation revision, field-level updates, no K writes). I recorded the minimal coordination requests in `.mvp-d-runtime/coordination-request.md` for the Codex supervisor to sync.
</p1>
<p2>
Fixed defect D-E2E-1: `assessment.analyze` now reconciles `reliable_new` against PG — if a member row already exists for `candidate_entity_id(ns, assessment_id)` (our prior enrollment succeeded despite a fresh process reporting reliable_new), it reuses that `member_id`, sets `identity_result.phase="enrolled_reconciled"`, and publishes; member-absent behavior unchanged. 95 tests, with a forced-failure check proving the new test covers the defect.

总协调 then issued a six-item ruling:

U: 必须纠正 requiredViews：failure_detail 已确认仅内部诊断列，数据架构通用约束禁止用于业务决策或跨服务协议，不得从它投影 requiredViews。

U: 暂不接受等待方案：正常缺少能力不得每30秒generation_revision+1并创建succeeded后继任务。

U: media.cleanup 明确属于MVP，归D补齐最小handler及验证证据…

It kept the namespace-level deterministic UUID serialization (don't change A's helper), forbade the failure_detail→requiredViews projection (move it into identity_result), rejected the wait-hop in favor of a lease-fenced deferral that keeps the same generation revision/logical task and doesn't consume an attempt, and assigned `media.cleanup` to D.
</p2>
<p3>
Fixed the reliable_new cross-cycle stall by reconciling against PG for an already-enrolled member instead of re-enqueuing forever. 总协调 then ruled: requiredViews must not come from failure_detail (move to identity_result), capability waiting must not bump generation_revision or spawn successor jobs (use lease-fenced deferral), and media.cleanup belongs to D.
</p3>
<p4>
D-E2E-1; enrolled_reconciled; requiredViews off failure_detail; media.cleanup to D
</p4>
</compartment>

<compartment start="59" end="69" title="Rulings 3/5: Java off failure_detail + orphan media.cleanup enqueue" episode_type="bug,feature" importance="76">
<p1>
I had the Java lane implement rulings 3 and 5. For ruling 3, `AssessmentRepository.ViewRow` dropped `failureDetail` and added `identityResult` (findById selects `identity_result::text`, no longer `failure_detail`), and I removed the unused `failure_code`/`failure_detail` from `AcceptanceRow`/`findByIdForUpdate` too, so Java reads `failure_detail` nowhere (grep-verified; it is still cleared to NULL on retake, which is an allowed write). `FailureProjection` was rewritten: `requiredViews(status, identityResultJson)` reads `identity_result.quality.required_views` only when `status='needs_retake'`, filters to `[front,left,right]`, dedupes and caps at 3, malformed/missing → empty; `retryable(failureCode)` is a closed mapping (null → null, any non-null → false). `AssessmentReadService` wires both; `failureCode` is still emitted verbatim from `failure_code`.

For ruling 5, the new `MediaCleanupEnqueuer.enqueueOrphansFor(UUID t13RequestId)` selects `id FROM media_objects WHERE request_id=? AND assessment_id IS NULL AND state IN ('pending','available','failed')` and enqueues each mediaId in its own fresh TransactionTemplate transaction as `job_type='media.cleanup'`, `owner_type='media'`, `owner_id=mediaId`, `input_revision=1`, dedup `media:{id}:cleanup:1`, payload exactly `{schema_version:1, media_object_id, cleanup_revision:"1"}` (matching `payload-media-cleanup.json`, additionalProperties:false); every exception is caught → `log.warn`, never rethrown. `AssessmentAcceptanceService` calls it on rejection (finish), on any business-tx RuntimeException (covers StaleAttemptException/INTERNAL rollback) and on media-intake failure. Happy path claims all media → enqueues nothing. Tests: 179 green, with orphan-cleanup assertions for DEVICE_OCCUPIED, replaced-view retake and the incomplete-view rollback path.
</p1>
<p2>
Java rulings 3/5: `AssessmentRepository.ViewRow` now carries `identityResult` instead of `failureDetail` (Java reads failure_detail nowhere; still cleared to NULL on retake), and `FailureProjection` takes `requiredViews` from `identity_result.quality.required_views` (needs_retake only, filtered to front/left/right, deduped, capped 3) with a closed `retryable` mapping (non-null → false). New `MediaCleanupEnqueuer.enqueueOrphansFor(t13RequestId)` enqueues one `media.cleanup` job per unowned media row (owner_type='media', dedup `media:{id}:cleanup:1`, payload `{schema_version:1, media_object_id, cleanup_revision:"1"}`), each in its own fresh tx with exceptions swallowed to warn; wired into the rejection, business-tx-rollback and media-intake-failure paths. 179 tests.
</p2>
<p3>
Java moved requiredViews onto `identity_result.quality` and stopped reading `failure_detail` entirely; added `MediaCleanupEnqueuer` to enqueue `media.cleanup` for orphaned media on rejection/rollback/intake-failure.
</p3>
<p4>
MediaCleanupEnqueuer; media:{id}:cleanup:1; requiredViews via identity_result.quality
</p4>
</compartment>

<compartment start="70" end="92" title="Public defer interface + C/D capability contract + cleanup orphan discovery" episode_type="design,feature" importance="74">
<p1>
总协调 opened this round with a C/D capability-linkage requirement, asking me to record the minimal final convention in `.mvp-d-runtime/coordination-request.md` and align it with the actual implementation rather than claim a frozen draft. The verified field paths: `plan_generate._build_input_snapshot` carries `schema_version`; `report.{assessment_id,report_id,report_photo_version}`; `capability.{microcrystal_id,capability_id,capability_revision,parameter_ranges}`; `model.{plan_provider,model_version,prompt_template_version}`; there is no top-level `required_capability_revision`. `capability_revision` comes from the approved baseline revision, not the selected device's observation generation; `microcrystal_id` is the generation source and does not bind execution to the original device; each `parameter_ranges` entry has `unit/min/max`; execution parameters live in `plan_payload.steps[].{region,parameters}`. D's own capability-selection draft still filtered on capability_id and revision>=baseline, with no actual parameter-coverage check, and the snapshot had not frozen `approved_regions`/`n_bounds`.

U: 请明确C字段路径与兼容覆盖规则；capability_revision只作来源追溯或明确批准兼容性判断，不以数值相等或变化直接拒绝；不要把旧草稿误报冻结完成。

Meanwhile the Python lane returned its rulings 3/4/5 work (107 passed): `requiredViews` flows only through `identity_result.quality` with `failure_detail` reduced to `{"reason": …}`; the wait-hop was deleted and replaced by an in-handler, lease-fenced polling wait with `MVP_D_PLAN_MAX_ATTEMPTS=2000`; and a `media.cleanup` handler was implemented and registered.

总协调 then issued a new authorization that replaced that interim wait:

U: D被指定为本次唯一公共Python队列defer接口及相关必要测试负责人…可最小新增complete_deferred或等价完成接口…立即撤销3600s handler阻塞等待及max_attempts=2000过渡补丁。增加等待不耗预算、真实失败耗预算、旧lease/重复defer拒绝、业务与队列原子回滚的必要证据。

The fix-4 lane delivered exactly that. `runtime/complete.py` gained `complete_deferred(engine, claim, *, defer_seconds, business_tx=None)` with the `_DEFER` SQL (same job/dedup, clears `lease_owner`/`lease_until`, moves `available_at`, refunds one attempt via `GREATEST`, bumps `lease_revision`, preserves `generation_revision`, and rejects an old or duplicate lease); `runtime/loop.py` added the defer dispatch branch; `handlers/__init__.py` added `HandlerResult.defer_seconds`. D-owned sources: `plan_generate.py` gained `_wait_guard`/`_frozen_rules`/`_covers_baseline`, froze `approved_regions`/`n_bounds` into the input snapshot, and deleted `_await_capability`; `media_cleanup.py` gained `discover_and_enqueue_orphans` (bounded single-table scan, reuses `_cleanable`/`_processor_active`/`_referenced`, idempotent dedup `media:{id}:cleanup:1`). The 3600s wait and 2000 max_attempts were removed. 125 tests green; a follow-up audit pass confirmed the four defer evidence classes and six discovery requirements with no defects.
</p1>
<p2>
总协调 fixed the C/D capability contract: `capability_revision` is source traceability from the approved baseline (not an equality gate); `parameter_ranges` carry unit/min/max; execution parameters live in `plan_payload.steps[].{region,parameters}`; D must freeze `approved_regions`/`n_bounds`. The Python lane had delivered rulings 3/4/5 (requiredViews via `identity_result.quality`, `media.cleanup` handler, wait-hop removed). 总协调 then designated D the sole owner of the public defer interface: add `complete_deferred` (verify running/owner/lease_revision/live lease/business input+generation_revision; atomically requeue the same job, move `available_at`, clear claim fields, refund one attempt, no negative; duplicate/old lease fail), revoke the 3600s in-handler wait and `MVP_D_PLAN_MAX_ATTEMPTS=2000`, and add cleanup orphan discovery/enqueue with `--once` evidence. Delivered in `runtime/complete.py`/`loop.py`/`handlers/__init__.py` plus `plan_generate.py` (`_wait_guard`, frozen `approved_regions`/`n_bounds`) and `media_cleanup.discover_and_enqueue_orphans`; 125 tests green, audit found no defects.
</p2>
<p3>
Established the public worker defer interface `complete_deferred` — a lease-fenced atomic requeue that keeps the same job/dedup and generation revision without consuming an attempt — aligned the C/D capability contract (revision = traceability, parameter coverage by unit/region/params), and added cleanup orphan discovery.
</p3>
<p4>
complete_deferred; defer_seconds; discover_and_enqueue_orphans; capability_revision traceability
</p4>
</compartment>

<compartment start="93" end="113" title="D E2E smoke round 1 + commit 6b4f9ed + Oracle auth block" episode_type="feature" importance="52">
<p1>
With the defer work in the tree, the fix-6 lane ran the full D-package E2E smoke live against mvp-d-pg (55437), web@18087 and the worker `--once`: PASS on all steps a–i — M3-A01 202 → analyze → `identity.enroll` → cross-cycle reconcile (`enrolled_reconciled`) → frozen report → plan ready (target 30, K untouched, generation_revision 0) → query matrix (A03/A05 brief 200, A05 full 403, A06 rev 1, APP grant→A04) → replay 200 replayed=true → 409 PHOTO_VERSION_CONFLICT → 409 DEVICE_OCCUPIED → 3 cleanup jobs → media deleted. Evidence written to `.mvp-d-runtime/e2e-evidence.md`, tree frozen start=end.

I then spawned Oracle R1 (M3) and R2 (M4+defer). All four attempts failed with the same minimal error, `Provided authentication token is expired`, over 10+ minutes. I recorded `oracleReview=blocked` (not passed), stopped retrying per the gate discipline, and verified the disk state — the LSP "duplicate method" reports were Eclipse JDT phantom index noise (each method has exactly one definition). I committed the D code as `6b4f9ed` (feature/mvp-assessments, 48 files +9322/−47: Java assessments package + the two stub files + Python four handlers/dshared + the three authorized shared defer files + tests; no contract/migration/other-package changes).
</p1>
<p2>
Ran the full D E2E smoke live (PASS a–i: acceptance→enroll→cross-cycle reconcile→frozen report→plan ready→query matrix→replay→PHOTO_VERSION_CONFLICT→DEVICE_OCCUPIED→cleanup). Then attempted Oracle R1/R2 four times — all failed `Provided authentication token is expired`; recorded the gate as blocked (not passed), no retry loop. Committed the D code as `6b4f9ed` (48 files).
</p2>
<p3>
Committed the D package code (`6b4f9ed`) after a passing live E2E smoke; the Oracle gate was blocked by an expired auth token and was not treated as passed.

<compartment start="114" end="124" title="Handoff reports D.md/D-oracle.md with Oracle BLOCKED" episode_type="docs" importance="45">

U: 请写并单独提交backend/handoffs/D.md与D-oracle.md，真实标Oracle BLOCKED、无结论，列实际oracle会话ID/候选代码SHA/最小错误（不含认证头cookie），保留待恢复后审查位置。

Test evidence was recorded as clean-tree SHA-bound reruns (Java 179/179, Python 125, contracts four scripts, all exit 0); the E2E was honestly disclosed as run on the pre-commit dirty `ccee6e2` tree, not as final-SHA proof.

<compartment start="125" end="141" title="Oracle R1 (ora-5) at 6b4f9ed + B1/B2/B3/I1/I2/I3/S1 fixes" episode_type="bug,feature" importance="80">
<p1>
